raw_response:
I have been farming these 3.5 mu for 30 years, same as my father did. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — that is how everyone here does it. I will stick with what works. Let me think through each crop.

**Wheat (winter, 3.5 mu):**
Last year I got around 480 kg per mu. I planted Jimai 22 — good variety, my neighbor Old Wang has been using it for five years and his yields are solid. I will use it again. Seeds cost me about 3 yuan per jin, I use about 25 jin per mu for drilling.

For fertilizer: at planting I put one bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu as base (that is 50 kg, so 7.5 N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K). Then at greening-up in spring I topdress with urea, about 20 kg per mu — that gives another 9 kg N. So total roughly 16-17 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. I would rather put a little extra than see yellow leaves — fertilizer is money but a bad harvest is worse.

Irrigation: 4 times usually — winter water (dong shui) before freeze, then at jointing, heading, and grain-filling. My well works fine. Pesticide: 2 sprays, one for aphids and powdery mildew around heading time, one earlier for weeds. Rotary tillage after maize harvest — nobody ploughs deep anymore, too expensive.

**Maize (summer, 3.5 mu):**
Right after wheat I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid — reliable, everyone around here uses it or similar. No-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble, saves time and money. Last year I got about 550 kg per mu.

Base fertilizer one bag of compound 15-15-15 per mu at planting, then urea topdressing at big trumpet stage, about 25 kg per mu. Total maybe 18 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K. Maize is hungry for nitrogen.

Summer rains usually cover most water needs but I irrigate once or twice if July is dry, especially around tasseling. One pesticide spray for corn borer and armyworm — this year the village warned us about fall armyworm so maybe two.

My family has 6 mouths, some work in the city, so the grain is mostly for us and some to sell. 3.5 mu is small — I cannot afford mistakes.
